title: Rogue changes: Protective Vanish, longer Sap, Gouge stops auto attack
changes: Smoke Veil is replaced by Protective Vanish: Vanish also makes you immune to damage and crowd control for 2 seconds, ending early if you leave stealth. Vanish no longer drops smoke.
Sap now reaches 7 yards, no longer takes you out of stealth, and ends on any damage.
Gouge now turns off your auto attack when it lands on an enemy.
Smoke clouds are much lighter to draw, which fixes the lag and crashes they caused.

title: Heal spam, lava, better line of sight, new cursors, and many fixes
changes: Fixed visual glitches on the Sandstone Yard in the lobby.
The scoreboard at the end of a match is gone: the match recap is the end screen now.
Flamestrike, Scorch and burning now use the same blazing flames as Fireball and Pyroblast.
Bots learn from many more kinds of mistakes (using trinkets, cooldowns, healing and defensive timing, target switching, movement and more), so they play smarter and keep improving.

Healing changes: dampening (heals getting weaker the longer a fight goes) is gone. Instead, pressing the same heal again and again now makes it weaker each time (15% less per repeat, down to 40% of full), while casting anything else in between (another heal or any other skill) keeps it at full strength; a short pause starts fresh.

Lava Forge's lava basins are now real lava: you can jump into one without being pushed out, but standing in it burns you (5% of your health every half second) and the rim holds you in, so you have to jump out.
Line of sight is more accurate: a unit whose edge shows past a pillar or wall corner can now be seen and targeted, as the picture shows, instead of reporting 'no line of sight'.

Pillars and cover now look exactly like what blocks you and your line of sight, so 'no line of sight' no longer shows up when you can plainly see your target (most of all on Cinder Crater, Lava Forge and Sandstone Yard).
The mage now stands up straight and in the middle of his own spot, and wings and cloaks sit properly on his back.
The mage's cloaks now recolour the back of his robe instead of adding a second cape.

New cursors: pick from a steel gauntlet and ten more to unlock; enemies always show a red sword, allies a green cross and aimed spells a crosshair. A Cursor section in settings has size, tint, trail and click ripple.

Switching maps in the lobby no longer makes your character slide away or sink through the floor: it stays on its spawn on every arena (including after picking Random), and party members always stand on free ground beside you.
The Rampager's greatsword now rests on his shoulder edge-on (the cutting edge toward you) instead of lying flat.
Bots were retrained for the new rules: healer bots now rotate their heals, use Pain Suppression more readily (even on themselves when dying), and warrior bots add Dragon Roar to their attacks.

Movement and combat feel smoother and more accurate online: other players are drawn closer to where they really are, your own character responds faster, and a lag spike no longer leaves your movement stuck behind for the rest of the fight.
New optional Network stats readout in the Esc menu settings: your ping, jitter and connection quality in the corner of the screen.

The error text (out of range, no line of sight...) is now bigger and easier to read, and both it and the stun/control text can be moved, resized and restyled in the HUD editor (colour, size, outline, background, how long it stays).
The Barbarian's polearm arm no longer looks stretched and torn around the shoulder: he holds it across the body with both hands in a natural pose.
Esc now always leaves the HUD editor, even right after picking something from a drop-down, and the Done button shows its key.
The network stats readout moved to the bottom right and can be moved, resized and restyled in the HUD editor, like the sound button, so nothing covers it any more.

The game server now supports a much higher update rate (62.5 instead of 20 updates a second) for tighter, more accurate fights, and other players are drawn closer to where they really are, so two screens agree on where each of you stands.

title: Three new arenas, wings, rogue and priest models, and a real Fireball
changes: Parties now start on the same team (until it is full) and the leader's Mode buttons wait, saying who is missing, until everyone in the party has pressed Ready; fixed a bug where a Ready press could be lost and leave the party stuck, and invites now say why they cannot go out.

The Friends window is tidier (friends grouped by what they are doing, a search box, avatars and clearer buttons), and the menu icons show how many friends are online, how many updates you missed in the patch notes, and how many matches you can watch.

The Rampager now carries his greatsword on his shoulder and grips it with both hands only when he attacks; the Barbarian holds a long polearm across his body, and the knight's armor no longer tears when he holds two-handed weapons.

Shouts, breaths and area spells now look like what they say: Dragon's Breath is a true cone of billowing flame (with embers, smoke and a glowing ground fan) that fills exactly the cone it hits, Dragon Roar breathes the same fire with sound waves, and Intimidating Shout and Psychic Scream send waves out from the caster's face and a shock ring out to their real radius. The caster throws their head back, chest out, and snaps forward as they shout. Cleave is a spinning blade round the warrior, Bladestorm and Slice and Dice keep blades whirling while they last, Reel In shows the cone it pulls from, Heroic Leap lands with a dust shockwave, and Vanish, Mirror Image, Evocation and Holy Nova have new bursts.

Fireball and Pyroblast are now real blazing fireballs: a white-hot core in rolling flames with a comet tail, embers and a glow on the ground, a fire burst and shock ring where they land, and Pyroblast grows in the mage's hand while it casts. Fireball and Pyroblast also have a new recorded launch and impact sound.
All cloaks now use a new draped cloth cape that sits properly on the back, sways as you move and turn, and takes the colour of each cloak skin.

The rogue is now a hooded shadow assassin who holds a curved dagger in each hand and strikes with them in turn, for every spec (Cutthroat, Duelist and Shade). Helmets, crowns and horns sit on top of the hood, capes replace the assassin's own coat, and dyes tint the whole outfit.

The priest is now an armoured sentinel in white and gold with a staff that matches your spec: Warden and Lightbearer carry a gold and white holy staff, Gloomweaver a necrotic staff topped with a glowing skull. Helmets, crowns and horns sit on top of the horned helm, capes replace the sentinel's own coat, and dyes tint the whole outfit.

Wings are now their own slot in the Look menu and replace the old shoulders (shoulder cosmetics are gone for now). All wings are built from one new feathered model that flutters when you stand, sweeps back and lifts when you run, beats when you jump, flares when you cast and folds when you fall, and fits every class. There are 10 styles: Angel, Duskwings, Phoenix and Verdant to start, then Emberwings, Frostfeather, Stormwings, Blossom, Voidwings and Solar Wings as you play more matches. Each has its own colours, glowing feather edges and effects such as drifting feathers, rising embers, falling frost, void wisps, lightning, petals, sun rays and stars. Wings and a cape can now be worn together. Wings you had saved on your back are kept; shoulder cosmetics are cleared.

Three new arenas: Cinder Crater, Lava Forge and Sandstone Yard. Each has plenty of cover to break line of sight (spires, jagged rock walls, brick chimneys, stacked carved blocks, lava basins and low barricades) and a raised ledge or plinth to fight over. Every older arena has been rebuilt with the same sharper stone, sand, ice and wood textures, better lighting, torches, banners and drifting dust, snow or embers, so all ten maps look alike in detail. The layouts of the old maps are unchanged.

Spells that need a spot on the ground (Flamestrike, Blizzard and the like) only show their aiming circle when you can actually cast them: it stays hidden while the spell is on cooldown, you are out of mana, or you are stunned or silenced, and says why.
Ice and arcane mage staffs now sit in the wizard's hand instead of floating beside it.

A big batch of new titles, icons and name colours to earn: 12 titles, 14 icons and 12 colours across matches played, wins and rating, from Regular and Victor to Grandmaster, Wolf, Scorpion, Ruby and Diamond.
New Brightness slider in the in-game settings menu (next to mouse sensitivity and volume) to make the picture darker or brighter; it is saved with your other settings.

title: An animated wizard mage and skill visuals that match what skills do
changes: The mage is now a fully animated old wizard with a staff to match your spec: Pyromancy has a fire staff and an ember-red robe, Cryomancy an ice staff and an icy blue robe, and Starweaving an arcane staff and a violet robe, each with its own glow. Hats, crowns and other cosmetics sit on the wizard, and dyes tint the robe.

Instant spells and damage-over-time effects now look like what they are: Scorch makes fire erupt at the target's feet instead of throwing a fireball, instant hits show their impact on the target, and damage-over-time and shield effects leave a lasting aura on the target (shadow swirls, bleeding drips, burning flames, frost shards, a golden shimmer) that flares on every tick. Real projectiles such as Frostbolt, Fireball and Smite still fly.

title: Slice and Dice holds its targets, a more natural Barbarian stance
changes: Slice and Dice is now a short-range lock-down: you stand in place and cut everything in the cone ahead in a flurry of fast strikes (16 quick hits for the same total damage), and everyone it hits is held in place for the whole channel with no gaps. You cannot move while it lasts, and being interrupted or stunned ends it.
The Barbarian stands more naturally: arms hang closer to the body and the feet are closer together, in idle, walking and fighting.

New skill visuals: Axe Throw is a real spinning axe with a trail (and Reel In a chain pulling the target in), Flamestrike is a swirling fire with embers, smoke and a pulse on every hit, Battle Banner and Not Going Anywhere plant a real waving flag, Rune of Power is a rotating rune circle with floating glyphs, and fire spells share one better flame effect. A falling-ice storm effect is ready for any frost ground spell.

Every warrior spec now uses the gold knight. Helmets, crowns, horns and other headwear you wear now sit on top of the knight's helm instead of replacing it, while shoulders and capes still replace the model's own pieces.

New weapons for the knight: Warbringer wields dual sabers, Rampager a greatsword and the Barbarian a two-handed axe, each held with both hands where it should be. See the new Credits link in the main menu for the artists.

Fixed dyes and cosmetic colours that looked almost black (Midas and Eclipse dye, several cloaks and wings) or washed out: Midas is a warm polished gold, Eclipse a deep violet with a glowing rim, and Aurora keeps its colour in shadow.
Model files are now packed so they cannot simply be downloaded and opened.

title: Five-tier talents, trinkets and class skills, target marks, new icons and cosmetics
changes: The talent tree is now five tiers. Tiers I and II are shared by all three specs of a class, tier III is your spec's own, tier IV is a trinket and tier V is a class skill. The old tiers IV to VI and their skill swaps are gone, and so are the skills only they gave (Smoke Bomb and the rest); your saved picks are cleared where they no longer exist.

Mage tier I changes Blink: Twin Blink (two charges, each on its own timer, with a number on the button for how many are ready), Blink and Cast (blink in the middle of a cast without losing it) or Frozen Departure (a Frost Nova where you stood). Tier II: 10% faster casts and global cooldown, 10% more health or 10% more damage. Tier III per spec: Frostbolt, Fireball or Arcane Blast do 10% more damage, plus a better chance of their proc, plus a 10% chance of an extra effect (root and Shatter, a 25 a second burn, free Arcane Power for 8 s or two Arcane Charges).

Warrior tier I changes Charge: a 2 second root after you arrive, 10 yards more reach, or Intercept (target an ally or yourself: rush to your ally, and they take 20% less damage for 4 s). Tier II: 20% attack speed, 10% health or 10% damage. Tier III per spec: Cleave, Bloodthirst or Deep Cuts do 10% more damage, 30% of their hits also Hamstring, and you gain 50% more rage.

Priest tier I changes Psychic Scream: 2 seconds longer, a 3 second stun in place on a 45 second cooldown, or targets flee as far from you as they can. Tier II: 10% faster casts, 10% more healing or 10% more damage. Tier III per spec: Penance (10% stronger, ticks every 0.25 s for 2.5 s with a barrier worth half of each tick's healing), Greater Heal (15% stronger, also heals you or your ally for 50% when you target the other, and a Renew on the target) or Mind Blast (10% stronger, a chance to make Devouring Plague free for 10 s, and a chance to slow 30% for 4 s).

Tier IV is a trinket for every class: an extra button beside the action bar, bound to F by default (change it under Controls). Choose Cleansing Charm (remove every harmful effect, even while stunned), Warding Charm (a shield worth 20% of your health for 8 s) or Healing Charm (heal 25% of your health). Each has a 60 second cooldown and no global cooldown.

Tier V gives each class a new skill in place of one it has. Warrior replaces Heroic Leap with Intimidating Shout (fear), Dragon Roar (a cone of dragon fire) or Battle Banner (you and your allies near it deal 10% more damage and take 10% less). Mage replaces Polymorph or Counterspell, your choice, with Mirror Image, Evocation or Rune of Power. Priest replaces Desperate Prayer (Warden, Lightbearer) or Power Word: Shield (Gloomweaver) with Leap of Faith, Purifying Light (an area dispel that blocks new debuffs) or Ascend to the Heavens (fly away, untouchable). Rogue replaces Sprint with Blind or Evasion, or learns Sap, which appears on the Kidney Shot button while you are stealthed. Duelist now starts with Gouge in place of Evasion.
All numbers on the new skills and trinkets are first guesses: expect them to be tuned over the next patches. Bots use every new skill and talent, and the tooltips and wiki cover them all.

Target marks: in Edit HUD there is a new Target group. Choose the arrow over your target (arrow, chevron, diamond, star, crosshair or none), its colour, size and movement, the circle under the target (ring, thin, thick, glowing disc or off) and how the target's health bars are highlighted.
The Watch live list now updates by itself while it is open: matches appear and disappear as they start and end.

Every skill and buff now has its own icon (no two skills share one any more). Fixed wrong or empty tooltip text on Mirror Image, Plague Ready, Purified, Ascended, Purifying Light, Penance Barrier and several talents.
New kill feed: who killed whom and with what, top right, fading after a few seconds. It can be moved and resized in Edit HUD and hidden under the Kill feed look option.
New match recap at the end of every match: damage, healing, damage taken, kills, deaths and biggest hit for everyone, with the most valuable player highlighted.
The trinket button is now a button of its own, apart from the action bar: move and resize it anywhere in Edit HUD.
The Look window no longer covers your character: it docks to the side, so you see each cosmetic on your character as you try it. Turn left and right, spin, and zoom to the head or weapon.

The warrior is now a detailed, fully animated gold-armoured knight with a horned helm. It walks, runs, strafes, casts, swings, jumps and falls, holds your spec's weapons, and the helmets, shoulders and capes you wear replace its own head, shoulder and coat pieces instead of stacking on top. Other classes keep their current look for now.

The warrior has new, fully animated 3D models. Warbringer and Rampager are a detailed gold-armoured knight with a horned helm, and the Barbarian is a spiked brute with a glowing-rune axe. They walk, run, strafe, cast, swing, jump and fall; the knight holds your spec's weapons; and the helmets, shoulders and capes you wear replace the model's own head, shoulder and coat pieces instead of stacking on top. Other classes keep their current look for now.

title: Resize your HUD, nameplate and health bar options, smarter bots
changes: Edit HUD: every element now has a corner grip. Drag it to change the width and height (double-click it for the natural size); frames stretch their health bars, the action bar wraps into rows, the combat log and cast bar take the new size. Scroll still scales, and sizes are saved with your layout.
New Health bars options in Edit HUD: bar height (thin to huge), ally and enemy health colours, and health text size.

New Nameplates options in Edit HUD: show them for everyone, enemies only, allies only or nobody; width; bar height; health text (percent or value); colour by team, class or health left; names on or off; text size; cast bars and debuffs on or off.
Windows like the spectator builds panel can be resized by dragging their corner.
Bots retrained, and they now also learn from matches between players: the losing classes learn from how the winners beat them.

title: Target arrow, raid marks, 6-player parties
changes: Your target now has a bobbing arrow over its head (red on enemies, gold on allies), so you always see who you are hitting.

Raid marks: put a Skull, Cross, Square, Moon, Triangle, Diamond, Circle or Star over anyone's head for your whole team. Right-click the target frame to pick one, or press Alt+1 to Alt+8 (Alt+0 clears; rebindable under Marks in Keybinds). Marking someone else with the same mark moves it; the same mark again takes it off.
Parties hold up to 6 players, so friends can play an in-house 3v3 with no bots: pick Team 1 or Team 2 in the party box (3 per side) and start a party match.
Long names in the party box no longer stretch the lobby; they are cut off with …

title: Smoke Bomb walls off sight, Recklessness swap
changes: Smoke Bomb now walls off sight at its edge: anyone outside the cloud cannot see or target an enemy inside it, and anyone inside cannot see or target an enemy outside. Enemies inside the same cloud see and fight each other as usual (it no longer blinds them), and allies are never hidden.
Rogue bots drop Smoke Bomb to cut off casters shooting them from range, and bots that lose sight of you walk into the cloud to find you.
Fury: the last talent row (Reckless Abandon, Stand Against Steel, Fortress Stance) now replaces Enraged Regeneration instead of Slam, so Slam stays on the bar.
Aura tooltips also name abilities that grant them on hit (Hot Streak from Flamestrike).

title: Dampening, smoke that hides, targeting fixes
changes: Dampening: from 90 seconds into a fight, all healing and new shields get 0.5% weaker every second (up to 90%), shown at the top of the screen. Two priests (or any healers) can no longer out-heal each other forever.

Smoke Bomb hides both ways: an enemy standing in the cloud cannot target anyone, and nobody outside it can target the rogue (or its partner) inside. Someone targeting them when they step in loses them, like losing a rogue to stealth, and bots go looking where they last saw them.
Bot priests break up enemy heals: a Psychic Scream or Hammer of Justice on an enemy who is casting a heal, unless their own side needs healing first.
Bots run out of an enemy's Bladestorm (or Slice and Dice) instead of standing in it trading swings, throwing instants on the way out.

Bots know which skills work on the move: while Bladestorm spins or Scorch casts they keep chasing, kiting, sidestepping and dodging instead of standing still, and a caster on the run counts Scorch as something to throw.
Ramps block sight like the solid wedges they are: standing on one, you cannot see (or be seen by) someone on the ground on its far side.
Bots stop a cast once its target has stepped out of sight, instead of finishing it into a pillar (stopping hands the global cooldown back, as it does for you).
Melee swings and melee skills no longer reach between floors: a bot (or you) on top of a walkway cannot hit someone on the ground just past its edge, and the other way round.

Play again against bots shows the arena you are really on. The menu backdrop could switch the scene back to the map picked in the menu while the next match loaded, so you saw one arena and bumped into another's walls.
A ground spell still on its cooldown no longer brings up its aiming ring (and an open ring goes away if the spell goes on cooldown).
Right-click never targets yourself, and holding a mouse button to steer or turn the camera is never taken as a click, however little the mouse moved.
Bots are named after their spec (Bot Rampager, Bot Pyromancy) so you can see what you are facing.
Watching a match or a replay shows a Builds panel on the right: every player's spec, skills and talents, with tooltips (N hides and shows it).
Patch notes show when each patch went out, in your own time zone.

title: Bots that move like players, warrior balance, clean-up
changes: Bots move like players: melee circles its target at speed instead of shuffling in place (with the odd hop), casters run from a melee that can still chase them and throw instants on the way, and stop to cast once it is slowed, rooted or left behind. Healing priests stand and heal.
Bots fake casts more: a kicker closing in counts as a threat, not only one already in reach.

Rogue bots spend combo points properly: Kidney Shot only with 4 or more and only while its stun lands in full, Eviscerate at 4 (at 3 on a target about to die). Before, Kidney Shot at 3 points ate every combo point.
Warrior bots use Heroic Leap to close any gap Charge cannot (on cooldown, no line of sight, too far), not only from beyond 25 yards.
Coming down from a jump on top of a barricade puts you beside it, never inside it (stopping mid-hop could leave you standing in the wall with sight both ways).

Bots hop over a barricade to shoot only when their global cooldown will be ready at the top of the jump, and never start a cast with a cast time in mid-air over one (it would fail when they land). Casters with their slowing spell ready (Frostbolt) stand and land it before they run.
Bot Shadow priests no longer recast Shadow Word: Pain on a low target every global cooldown (left over from when it was an execute).
Cleave: 75 damage (was 85) and 8 rage (was 15). Free rage from Cleave was feeding Mortal Strike nonstop; Warbringer won about nine in ten bot duels.
Rampager hits harder: Bloodthirst 150 damage (was 85), Slam 160 (was 120). It dealt about a third of Warbringer's damage.

Tooltips: Holy Nova says it heals you and every ally in range; Reel In says it drags every enemy hit; Bladestorm no longer says it cannot be stopped twice. Fortress Stance's buff is called Fortress Stance (was Shield Wall). The Charge stun and Hobbled have their own icons. Rampager has a sword icon.

Talent names and wording: Holy's Shadow Word: Pain talent is Lingering Shadow (was Final Verdict), the rogue Fan of Knives talents are Knife Flurry (was Blade Storm, easy to mix up with the warrior's Bladestorm), and two descriptions read more clearly.
The README now describes the person-high barricades and the practice bots' real reaction times and interrupt rates.

title: Person-high barricades, bots learn how people beat them
changes: Low barricades are now as tall as a person. On the ground you cannot see or cast past one. Jump and your line of sight rises over it for a moment: long enough for an instant spell from the top of the jump (both ways, so they can do it to you too). Spells with a cast time still need sight when they finish.
Jumps go higher (1.8 instead of 1.45) so you clear the taller barricades. How long you are in the air and when you clear rails, barricades and ground effects are unchanged.
Bots use barricades too: they hop and throw an instant over one when it is all that blocks the target, and count them as cover when they break line of sight.
Bot priests purge like players: with nobody low, they strip an enemy's Ice Barrier, Power Word: Shield, Power Infusion, Arcane Power or Evocation with Dispel Magic.
Slice and Dice cuts twice as often for half as much: 50 damage every 0.5 seconds (8 cuts, the first at once) instead of 100 every second. Same 400 in total, same 4-second hold.
Shadow Mend (rogue tier I talent) now heals 50% of your missing health when you vanish, down from 75%.
The spec card shows the spec you have picked. Hovering another spec previews it, and moving back to the talents or anywhere else returns the card to yours.

Another spec's card counts only talents you can see picked: the class tiers (I and II) you have now. Its own tiers are not counted until you pick that spec, so a talent you have not chosen (Crippling Technique on Hamstring, Leaping Strides on Charge and Heroic Leap) no longer shows as a buff. Switching specs keeps your tier I and II picks as shown and brings back that spec's own tiers as you left them.
Buff and debuff tooltips on someone else's effect show its plain values: your own talents only change the numbers of effects you put there.

Bots learn from how people beat them. After every match against people the server replays it and looks for the moments a person outplayed a bot: casts kicked while a kick was ready, kicks wasted on a fake, deaths with a big defensive still unused, deaths to a burst it never answered, long casts taken in the open, time in ground effects, a melee bot kited or a caster pinned. Each becomes a lesson for that class (losses count three times as much as wins). A lesson brain is tried after every match, and new brains are bred towards the lessons, so bots adapt within tens of games.
Bots also study how people kick and fake (how far into a cast people kick, when they stop a fake) and time their own fakes before that point.

title: Slice and Dice holds, cast bars say why, tooltips say where
changes: Slice and Dice holds its target for the whole channel: the first strike and its stun land the moment the spin starts, and each tick's stun lasts past the next, so there is no gap to walk out or swing back in. Diminishing returns shorten the hold as one block (at half, the target is held for the first two seconds, then free).

Cast bars show why a cast stopped: it stays up for a second, frozen where it stopped, labelled and coloured Interrupted (red), Crowd controlled or Pulled (purple), Cancelled or Moved (grey), or Line of sight, Out of range, Target lost, Smoked (orange). Yours, the unit frames' and the nameplates'.
Bladestorm is no longer ended by pressing another skill (a bot was cancelling its own spin with Pummel): your other skills wait until it is over.
Each spec's card and tooltip lists its passives: its built-in effect (Pyromancy's Cauterize), its weapon and auto-attack, and the bonuses it carries (Rampager's longer Bloodthirst and Slam).
Tooltips say where each bonus comes from: the spec's passive or a talent and its tier. A buff or debuff icon's tooltip says who put it on and what gives it (an ability, a spec passive or a talent).

Bots no longer see through stealth: when a rogue stealths or vanishes they lose it, go to where they last saw it and search the area around there, instead of walking straight to where it really is. A bot that has seen nobody holds its ground, and hidden enemies no longer count for its area spells or its running away.

title: Slice and Dice stuns and retrained bots
changes: Slice and Dice: one cast is one step of stun diminishing returns. Its first tick sets the level and every later tick of that cast stuns for that same full length; the next cast is halved throughout (before, each tick stepped the count down, so the third and fourth ticks barely stunned).

Bot brains retrained in 1v1, 2v2 and 3v3 on every arena with the new traits: how often they fake casts, how long they wait before kicking, how readily they break line of sight and how much they keep moving.

title: Smarter bots, learned rotations and balance
changes: Bots learned to juke: a caster may start a cast while your interrupt is ready and stop it part way, so a kick thrown at it is wasted; the real cast follows. Interrupting bots wait into a cast before kicking, and wait longer against someone who has faked them before.

Bots use line of sight: they step behind a pillar, a wall or a deck so a long cast at them (a Polymorph, a Pyroblast) fails, and take cover the same way when hurt, on both floors. They keep throwing instants on the way.
Bots take the ramp up to you when you stand on a walkway, instead of waiting underneath; a pillar between them and you counts as out of reach too, and they path round it.
Bots move more like players: they keep sidestepping between casts (never into a wall, out of sight or into a ground effect), hop now and then, and Normal bots decide more often.

Every spec's damage rotation is learned: the order of its skills that deals the most damage with the real cooldowns, costs, procs and combo points. Bots play it; finishers and rage dumps go off at their own thresholds.

Bots take talents, so every tier IV to VI skill gets played: Flamestrike, Blizzard, Arcane Silence, Evocation, Silence, Hammer of Justice, Power Infusion, Holy Word: Serenity, Knife Snipe, Crippling Strike and Fan of Knives are all used now, and a bot whose interrupt was swapped uses the new one.
Shadow priests with a partner fight instead of hanging back like a healer. Dispersion is kept for stuns, fears, sheep and low health, not any root.
High-ground mages climb all the way up (the foot of a ramp no longer counts) and give up the climb once melee reaches them. Bots jumping a barricade aim at its far side.
Difficulty means more: Easy reacts in about 1.3 s, skips a third of its decisions, interrupts rarely and saves itself late; Normal sits in between; Hard is unchanged.

Bot brains are trained in 1v1, 2v2 and 3v3 on every arena; brains stored by the server are completed from the trained baseline, so older ones no longer miss their emergency defensives, pre-shields and ground-effect dodging.
A cast you stop before it finishes (moving, stopping, faking) gives the global cooldown back. Interrupts and crowd control keep it.
Kidney Shot: 2 s plus 0.8 s per combo point, never longer than 6 s (was 3 s + 1 s per point, up to 12.2 s with talents).
Slice and Dice's stun is now in the stun diminishing-returns group; Charge's short stun has its own group.
Exsanguinate sets your bleeds to triple damage; using it again no longer multiplies them further.
Holy Nova reaches 12 yards (was 60). Ice Barrier absorbs 25% of maximum health (was 40%).
Friendly spells no longer need facing: shielding or healing an ally behind you works.
The same debuff or buff from two sources counts once: two Mortal Wounds or two Power Infusions no longer stack.

Talents re-pointed so tier I is never wasted: Combat's tier V and Subtlety's tier VI replace Sprint and Shadowstep instead of Vanish; Holy's tier V replaces Desperate Prayer and Shadow's tiers V and VI replace Dispersion and Mind Flay; the mage tier I talent Fleet Step speeds Blink (Polymorph is always swapped out at tier IV), and the warrior's Battle Rush improves Heroic Leap instead of Charge.

title: Client polish: sync, keys, pop-ups and small screens
changes: Settings sync is merged one setting at a time against what this browser last agreed with the server, kept per account: a device that synced once no longer overwrites what you changed on another device, and two accounts on one browser no longer share it. The server never drops your newest settings when you change things quickly.

In a match every bound key belongs to the game: Ctrl+R with R bound, Ctrl+S and the like no longer reach the browser. Binding a shortcut the browser always keeps (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Tab...) shows a warning, and reloading or closing the page mid-match asks first.

Nameplates and floating numbers from the last match are cleared when it closes, you disconnect or you stop watching. The end screen (Ready / Leave and the scoreboard) is hidden when the connection drops.

One pop-up manager: Escape closes the window on top (Friends, Watch live, suggestions, profile, the look picker, the spec card), even while typing or after touching a slider, without opening the settings menu behind it. A match starting closes every pop-up, the settings menu and the HUD editor.
Flamestrike, Blizzard and the banner can be aimed while you are casting something else, and placing one during a cast or the global cooldown queues it.
HUD positions are saved as fractions of the screen and fitted onto it whenever the HUD appears, so a layout made on a big screen never leaves the action bar off the edge of a laptop.
Joining a duel uses the class and build picked in the menu for the tooltips and the bar.
Guests have a name field again (it was removed but still read, so every guest was 'Player').
Small screens: the help text and combat log stay clear of the action bar, the main menu fits 1280x720 without scrolling, and the header icons stay in the corner below 1100 px wide.
Hints name the keys you bound (auto-attack, switching who you follow) instead of R and Tab.
Buff and debuff icons are only redrawn when they change, not every frame.

title: Combat fixes and an unstoppable Bladestorm
changes: Bladestorm cannot be interrupted, and while it spins the warrior is immune to stuns, fears, incapacitates, roots, slows and Reel In. Bots no longer waste a kick on it.
Kicking a warrior's physical channel (Slice and Dice) now only locks that ability, not every physical skill.
Kidney Shot's combo-point time is part of the stun, so diminishing returns now shorten all of it (the second stun is half, the third a quarter).
Dispel Magic takes crowd control off an ally first; a damage-over-time effect no longer sorts ahead of a sheep or a fear.
Deep Freeze taken as a Fire or Arcane talent works without Fingers of Frost or Shatter (nothing on those bars can apply them).
Range talents for cone and area abilities make them reach further: Reel In's +4 yards now works.
A feared unit that is also rooted or stunned stays put instead of walking.
Area attacks (Psychic Scream, Shockwave, Reel In, Holy Nova, Bladestorm and the rest) need line of sight and are measured in 3D: no more screams through a pillar or shockwaves through the deck.
Heroic Leap's landing damage is measured in 3D and needs line of sight.
Shadowstep to someone at the edge of a walkway lands on the walkway, never in the air off its edge.
Only direct damage stops a Charge: a damage-over-time tick no longer cancels it and wastes the cooldown.
A Charge at someone up on a walkway ends underneath without the hit (and without leaving its stun behind).
Reel In pulling someone off a walkway puts them on the ground.
Vanish cancels a Charge already on its way to you.

Tooltip and talent text: Enraged Regeneration lists its Bloodthirst heal, Blizzard talents no longer promise a slow, Evocation is described as it works (6 s of fast mana regeneration), and the Vanish smoke cloud says what it does.

title: Ranked and server safety
changes: Ranked is for signed-in players only. Guests still have Find match, an unrated queue of their own that never meets the ladder.
One account in two windows can no longer be queued against itself, and an account already playing in another window cannot join the queue or a duel.
Signing out during a ranked match (or while queued) is refused. Leaving a live ranked match is a loss charged to the account that started it, even if that session has ended meanwhile.

Leaving a ranked match during the countdown calls the match off: everyone else goes back to the front of the queue (parties together) and nobody loses rating. The leaver cannot queue ranked for a minute.
Ranked Play again only rematches the full roster. If someone has left, pressing it puts you back in the ranked queue instead of a short-handed match.
You can no longer join a practice, the queue or watch a match while you are waiting for a duel to start (it used to put you in two matches at once).
Spectators are told when a match closes because everyone left the end screen (they used to be stuck, and showed as busy to friends).
A declined, expired or withdrawn party invite no longer leaves you in a party of one that blocked duel invites.
A stealthed rogue's own casts, buffs and turns are no longer sent to the enemy team while it is hidden.
Stealth detection is measured in 3D: a rogue on the deck right above you is no longer 'within 2 yards'.
The leaderboard is cached for 10 seconds and read in one batch; each connection can only have a few account requests waiting, and none run after it closes.
Per-address limits use the address the host's proxy saw, not one the client can make up. Failed logins are also limited per account name.
Every change to an account (results, friends, settings, looks, icons) is written one at a time, so a friend request can no longer erase a recorded win.
The bots' study of each finished match now runs on a worker thread, so long matches no longer freeze every room for up to several seconds.

Replays: refused button presses are no longer recorded, so long matches stay well under the size limit. Solo practice is not stored (ranked, party and duel matches are), and if a replay is still too big you are told.
Suggestions are limited per account and per network (reconnecting no longer resets the limit), and old rate-limit entries are forgotten.
Pressing the spell you are already casting no longer restarts it; near the end of the cast it is queued to go off right after.

title: Leap up, look down, new features on every map
changes: Heroic Leap aimed on top of a walkway (a deck or a ramp) lands up there instead of on the ground below. Aiming any ground spell now picks the surface you point at, deck or ground.
A raised deck is a floor between levels: someone above you is hidden while the deck is between you, and you see them again once you can look past its edge.
Ground spells only reach the floor they were placed on: a Flamestrike on the deck no longer burns people underneath it, and the other way round. Bots aim theirs at their target's floor.
Barricades are chest-high now and longer, and need most of a jump to clear (rails still need only a hop).
Dusk Colosseum: an emperor's box on the north and south walls, each a small raised balcony with a ramp at each end.
Sunken Ruins: two crumbling stone platforms climb out of the rubble (replacing the two small columns north and south), and two broken walls you can vault.
Frostkeep Pit: a frozen bridge spans the pit from north to south through the ring of spires, and snowdrift walls guard the flanks.
Heroic Leap is a real leap on your own screen too: your character arcs up and lands on the spot (before, only others saw the arc).
The header icons on the menu are coloured: gold profile, green friends, blue patch notes, red watch live, yellow suggestions.
Training dummies come back fresh: no leftover diminishing returns or combo points after they stand up.
Fix: a malformed web address could crash the server for everyone; it now gets an error page.

title: Jump off the walkway, three new arenas
changes: Walkways: walking still stops at the rails, but a jump clears them and you drop to the ground. You can also jump onto the lower half of a ramp from the side.
The Serpent: the walkway is wider (6 yards) and now the same run for both teams, with one more pillar on each side underneath for cover.

Twin Ramps is gone. New arenas: The Overlook (a raised plateau with ramps north and south and a shaded hall underneath; every duel is played here), Icebound Ring (a raised square ring around an open courtyard) and Sun Terraces (two long raised terraces along the walls).
Low barricades: they block walking but not sight, and you can jump over them.
Range is measured in 3D: up on a walkway you are out of melee reach from the ground below.
Charge and Heroic Leap clear rails and barricades, so Charge can take you off a walkway onto someone below. Shadowstep lands you on your target's level.
Bots find their way on every map: they climb ramps, jump off walkways and hop barricades.
Lobby: drag on the empty middle of the menu to turn your character.

Menu: the spec card stays open while your mouse is on that side, so you can reach it from any spec. Skill tooltips on the menu show your talents' numbers as you pick them (changed numbers in green with the base value struck through), and the card flags skills your talents change or add.
Tooltips say each thing once, and every skill shows how long its effects last, what it costs and what it generates (for example the 8 s banner of You're Not Going Anywhere).
Fix: a talent that lowers a spell's cost now also counts when the cast finishes, so the spell no longer fails with too little mana at the end.
The site has its own icon, and links to the game show a preview card.
The README is now a player guide, with a full skills and talents wiki (WIKI.md).

title: The Serpent walkway
changes: The Serpent is now a raised, winding wooden walkway between the two start yards: a ramp up from each side, an S-shaped deck, and open ground with stone piers underneath.
The deck is a ceiling for line of sight; the ramps and piers are solid on the ground, and rails keep you on the walkway.
Bot mages sometimes climb to the walkway and fight from the high ground.
Talents are now remembered per spec: switch spec or class and your picks are still there.
Esc opens the game menu in the lobby too (Controls, HUD layout, sound).
Auto-attack no longer switches itself off while you still have an enemy targeted, so it is there when you close in or use a skill.
Practice against dummies: a fallen dummy stands back up at full health after a moment instead of ending the match.

title: One look for the whole UI
changes: Main menu right side is now a Look card and a Match panel (1v1/2v2/3v3 buttons, arena and bot skill rows, partners under Advanced).
New Look menu: slots on the left, options as a grid, locked looks show how many matches they need.
Spec popup shows its 8 skills as tiles you drag to reorder; the character panel uses spec chips and a text talent tree.
Esc menu, Controls, patch notes and tooltips restyled to match: tinted header strip, stat chips, gold frames.

title: Menu overhaul, new look and The Serpent
changes: New main menu: ARENA title, icon header (profile, friends, patch notes, watch live, suggestions) and a lobby party roster showing class, spec, side and ready state.
Drag skills in the Skill bar order strip to rearrange your bar; each slot shows its key and the match uses your order.
Hold Alt over a skill for an in-depth tooltip: how damage is built, what boosts it and diminishing returns. Rebind it in Controls.
Suggestions and Watch live now require signing in. Drop a .txt file on the suggestion box for longer ideas.
Twice the cosmetics: new unlockable looks earned by matches played.
HUD editor works from the main menu with a grid, snapping and many more frame and bar looks.
Sound revamp: every ability has its own cast, impact and ambient voices, plus footsteps per arena, low-health heartbeat and landings.
New arena The Serpent: two interlocking walls form an S-shaped corridor. Bots navigate around walls.

title: Patch notes
changes: New Patch notes list in the main menu showing every recent patch.

title: Pyroblast, mana and smarter retreats
changes: Pyroblast now hits for 550.
A fully cast Pyroblast always grants Hot Streak (the free instant one does not chain into another).
Mana regeneration: mage 12 → 24 per second, priest 6 → 15.
Bots look ahead for walls when backing away or running to cover and slide along them instead of getting stuck.
Bot mages Blink toward open ground, never into a wall, and cast Hot Streak Pyroblast first.

title: Play again and bot fixes
changes: Play again against bots always picks a different map and a different enemy class.
Bots no longer spin in circles: fixed the mage Blink-turn loop, rogue circling, tight melee strafing and ramp-foot wobble.
Bots respect diminishing returns and existing crowd control, hold burst for targets without defensives, and only interrupt casts that matter.
Bot brains retrained.

title: Bots that care for their lives
changes: Bots use defensive spells, shields and escapes earlier, step out of Flamestrike and Blizzard, and keep their own shield up.
Bots learn from how close matches were, not only from wins and losses.
Play again against bots picks a random enemy class.

title: Twin Ramps with a tunnel
changes: Twin Ramps rebuilt: a raised bridge deck with a ramp at each end and a walkable tunnel underneath, with line-of-sight rules for each level.
Specs no longer carry stat bonuses, so damage is flat for testing.
Casting needs the target within a 180° cone; Dragon's Breath is a 90° cone.
Walking backwards is 75% speed.
Pyromancy gets Cauterize: dropping to lethal damage leaves you at 35% health (3 minute cooldown).

title: Twin Ramps duel map
changes: New Twin Ramps duel map with a chasm, two ramps and a bridge. Duels are played there.
Rage gained from damage taken is halved.

title: Rage and tooltips
changes: Mortal Strike spends rage instead of generating it, and spenders no longer refund rage.
Tooltips say exactly what a spell deals.
The match countdown is 5 seconds.

title: Exact damage
changes: Damage has no random variance: every hit does exactly what the tooltip says.
No Blink while disoriented by Dragon's Breath.
Ground spells that cannot land are not cast, so no wasted cooldown.

title: Ground spells feel better
changes: Flamestrike can be cast in any direction, and the aim dot is coloured by line of sight.
Ground spells cast on mouse down instead of release.

title: Priest and mage fixes
changes: Devouring Plague's first hit no longer breaks fear.
Ice Barrier absorbs 40% of max health.
Dragon's Breath disorients and cannot be escaped with Blink.

title: Frost tweaks
changes: Frost Nova grants Fingers of Frost.
Ice Lance has a 1 second cooldown.
Mind Blast hits for 340.

title: Talent rows and random duel map
changes: New talent row pattern, plus frost, priest and warrior changes.
Suggestions can carry notes.
Duels use a random map.

title: Menu tidy
changes: Suggestions can be deleted and the menu corner is tidier.

title: Suggestions to Discord
changes: Suggestions are sent to a Discord webhook.
Kick and Pummel can miss.

title: Suggestion box
changes: New suggestion box in the menu.
Counterspell can whiff.

title: Barbarian and Arcane
changes: Barbarian: Reel In pulls enemies in a cone, Deep Cuts generates rage and Axe Throw is buffed.
Arcane Barrage deals +75% per Arcane Charge.

title: Rematch ready check
changes: Everyone readies up on the end screen to play again.
Bots learn from human replays.
Mage and warrior tweaks.

title: Hot Streak procs
changes: Fireball, Flamestrike and Dragon's Breath each have a 15% chance to grant Hot Streak.
End-of-match Play again and Leave buttons; shorter spec descriptions.

title: Cryomancy rework
changes: Cryomancy reworked around Fingers of Frost and Shatter.
Heroic Leap is a real jump.
You keep your party when leaving a match.

title: Warrior rework
changes: Warriors share Charge, Pummel, Hamstring and Heroic Leap.
New Warbringer, Rampager and Barbarian kits.

title: Party lobby
changes: The lobby shows every party member with a name tag and ready check.

title: Party looks
changes: Party members' models and skins show in the lobby.

title: Shadowstep and reconnect
changes: Shadowstep lands behind the target and turns your camera.
Reconnect after matches; unsynced settings are kept.

title: Rogue rework and learning bots
changes: Rogue rework.
Bots learn from the matches they play.
Louder party invites.

title: Warrior spec swaps
changes: Mortal Strike and Bloodthirst swap between warrior specs.
Bots play the spec they are given.
The end scoreboard closes when a new match starts.

title: Warrior weapons
changes: Warrior specs are weapons: dual wield, two-handed sword and polearm.

title: End scoreboard
changes: A scoreboard at the end of every match.
Warrior damage up about 30%.

title: Camera and shield bar
changes: Steadier camera under crowd control.
The shield bar is visible and white.

title: Spell queue and spectating
changes: The queue only repeats a spell in its last 0.25 s; conditional skills are blocked.
